clue.text: Splendid 4-0 result, you say? Worthless!

parts.note: splendid and good both mean excellent

indicators.note: what you say is heard rather than read, so the digit is taken as its spoken word

parts.note: the number spoken matches a common preposition
a zero is nothing

explanation.surface: A football fan hears a four-nil scoreline, then scoffs that it was worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: Read a 4-0 result out loud as 'good, four, nothing' and the spoken four becomes the preposition in the hyphenated phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A good-for-nothing person or thing is useless, of no value at all, which is what worthless says.

clue.text: Hale goes to kick Dicky, disappearing fast

indicators.note: dicky means faulty or unsound, so the words before it are broken up and rebuilt

parts.note: the four words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A footballer called Hale lines up to take a kick at someone named Dicky.
explanation.walkthrough: Dicky looks like a name, but it is British slang for shaky or not working properly, the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods that go like hot cakes sell out very quickly, an idiom for vanishing from the shelves rapidly.

clue.text: Heart, for example, in charge, which is natural

parts.note: the heart is one example of a body organ
IC is the standard abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A medical note about a heart being in charge of something natural.
explanation.definitionFit: Organic food or farming is produced naturally, without artificial chemicals, so the adjective is a synonym.

clue.text: Pays for implement to make piece of furniture

parts.note: to foot the bill is to pay for it
a tool is an implement

explanation.surface: Someone buys a tool in order to build a piece of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A footstool is a low stool for resting the feet on, a small item of household furniture.

clue.text: Resign, as inclusion involves a second transfer

definitions.note: a noun phrase for the act; the answer is the verb, to transfer a second time

indicators.note: inclusion means being taken inside, so the short word goes within the first one

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An employee told to resign is instead moved sideways to another post.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as part of the instructions, but 'a second transfer' describes the answer: re- plus assign.
explanation.definitionFit: To reassign is to assign again, moving someone to a new post one more time, so a repeat transfer.

clue.text: Element producing no information about two unknown characters

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the outer words wrap round the pair of characters

parts.note: O looks like a zero, nothing
gen is British slang for information
in algebra x and y are the usual unknowns

explanation.surface: A chemistry puzzle: an element yielding no data about two mystery letters.
explanation.walkthrough: No information is O plus GEN, and the two algebraic unknowns sit between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxygen is a chemical element, number eight in the periodic table, so the answer is an example.

clue.text: Ladies' quarters are taken over by the Queen

indicators.note: something taken over is held within another, so the royal letters surround the word

parts.note: HM stands for Her Majesty
taken as written

explanation.surface: Royal apartments for women have been commandeered by the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A harem is the separate part of a Muslim household reserved for the women, their living area.

clue.text: Disgusting sound heard by a few

indicators.note: heard means listened to, so the pieces are joined by how they are spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a noise is a sound
some means a few

explanation.surface: A revolting noise was heard by a handful of people.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken together, noise and some run their S sounds into one and give the answer's pronunciation.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisome means offensive or foul-smelling, nothing to do with noise, so it is a synonym of disgusting.

clue.text: Silly mistake: fathered English bairn

indicators.note: a mistake puts things wrongly, so the following letters are muddled

parts.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English
taken as written; a bairn is a Scottish child

explanation.surface: Someone foolishly fathered a child with an English person, a silly error.
explanation.definitionFit: A featherbrained person is scatty and foolish, as if their head held only feathers, so it means silly.

clue.text: A line follows host and old soldier

indicators.note: coming after places these pieces behind the first word in sequence

parts.note: a host and a legion are both a vast number
taken as written
RY is short for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A queue forms behind the host and a veteran soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A legionary was a soldier of a Roman legion, a fighting man from ancient times.

clue.text: Breed of artist is English

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A painter's breed or pedigree turns out to be English.
explanation.walkthrough: Breed reads as a noun, a kind of animal, but it is the verb, as in breeding cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise animals or children is to rear them, which is what breed means as a verb.

clue.text: Royal books?

parts.note: surface reading: books owned by or about royalty
setter's reading: two books of the Old Testament whose name is a word for monarchs

explanation.walkthrough: The Bible has two books named after rulers, chronicling the monarchs of Israel and Judah.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old Testament books named for monarchs are literally royal books, a Bible reference.

clue.text: Boast about team engaged in craft

indicators.note: engaged in means occupied inside, so one word goes within the other
about can mean around and about, astray, so the first word is jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A crew brags about their team taking part in some boating.
explanation.definitionFit: A steamboat is a vessel driven by steam power, and a craft is any boat or ship.

clue.text: Spasm causing minor difficulty

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an involuntary jerk of the diaphragm
second meaning: a small hitch or setback

explanation.surface: A sudden twitch creates a small problem for someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiccough, an old spelling of hiccup, is both the jerky catch in breathing and a slight temporary snag.

clue.text: Said to feel cold on the border

indicators.note: said means spoken out, so the word wanted is one that sounds like the following phrase

parts.note: to freeze is to feel very cold

explanation.surface: Someone complains of feeling chilly out on the frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: A frieze is a decorative horizontal band along the top of a wall, a kind of ornamental strip or edging.

clue.text: Unusual impression given by in Parma, perhaps

definitions.note: the clue as published has lost a word here, so this phrase no longer reads as a definition

parts.note: rare means unusual, seldom met
a stamp is a mark pressed into something, an impression

explanation.surface: A collector's odd postmark comes from someone in the Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue as published is a word short. Unusual plus impression builds the answer plainly; the tail most likely read 'given by rest in Parma, perhaps', an anagram of rest and Parma, and a lost word leaves it garbled.
explanation.definitionFit: A stamp scarce enough to prize is a rare stamp, the kind a philatelist hunts for, perhaps an Italian issue.

clue.text: Move close to a very quiet swimmer …

parts.note: taken as written
pp, pianissimo, is the musical mark for very quiet
the roach is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Someone edges silently towards a swimmer in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: Swimmer is crossword shorthand for a fish; the ellipsis carries the scene on into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To approach something is to come nearer to it, the same verb as moving close to.

clue.text: Get to grips with tools

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to deal with a problem or opponent
second meaning: equipment, especially for fishing

explanation.surface: Someone sets about mastering their equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: To tackle a task is to engage with it, and fishing tackle is a word for gear or equipment.

clue.text: … in case rogue's caught in waterfall

indicators.note: something caught is held inside a trap, so the villain sits within the first word

parts.note: taken as written
a cad is a dishonourable man, a rogue

explanation.surface: Continuing from the swimmer: a villain is trapped in a box in a waterfall.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'in' finishes the sentence from the previous clue and plays no part here.
explanation.definitionFit: A cascade is a small waterfall, especially one of a series falling over rocks, so it is a synonym.

clue.text: Endless crispbread crushed for pork dish

indicators.note: crushed things are broken up, so the remaining letters are rearranged
without ends, so the opening and closing letters are dropped from the word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Broken crackers are crumbled up to coat a pork dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A sparerib is a cut of pork ribs with most of the meat trimmed off, often served barbecued.

clue.text: About abandoning dreadfully neurotic habit

indicators.note: dreadfully suggests things in a terrible state, so the letters are muddled
abandoning means leaving behind, so the small piece is removed from the word

parts.note: c, short for circa, means about
taken as written

explanation.surface: An anxious person tries to give up a dreadful habit.
explanation.definitionFit: A routine is a regular, customary way of doing things, so a habitual pattern.

clue.text: New nun goes round diocese, remaining out of sight

indicators.note: going round something means surrounding it, so the church district sits inside
new means made afresh, so the following word is reordered

parts.note: taken as written
a see is a bishop's diocese

explanation.surface: A newly arrived nun tours the diocese without anyone noticing her.
explanation.walkthrough: New looks like an adjective for nun, but it rearranges the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Unseen means not observed, hidden from view, which is the sense of out of sight.

clue.text: One sits on the fence or a bannister, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps marks one possible arrangement, so the preceding words are rearranged

parts.note: the stair rail, spelt here with a doubled N; the usual one-N spelling banister is what the letters need

explanation.surface: Someone perched on a fence, or a stair rail, refusing to choose.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram needs the usual spelling banister with one N; the printed variant bannister leaves a spare N.
explanation.definitionFit: Sitting on the fence is an idiom for refusing to take sides, just as an abstainer declines to vote.

clue.text: A plank seen from the middle of the boat

definitions.text: from the middle of the boat

parts.note: taken as written
a beam is a long thick piece of timber, a plank

explanation.surface: A sailor spots a plank floating level with the middle of the boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Abeam is nautical for at right angles to a ship's keel, directly out to the side from its midpoint.

clue.text: South African girl in steam bath

parts.note: SA is the abbreviation for South Africa
Una is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman from South Africa relaxes in a steam room.
explanation.definitionFit: A sauna is a Finnish-style hot room where people sit and sweat, a kind of steam bath.

clue.text: Avoid first lady to receive notice

indicators.note: receiving something takes it in, so the short word goes inside the name

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in Genesis
an ad is a notice, an advertisement

explanation.surface: Dodging the President's wife who is to be served with a notice.
explanation.walkthrough: First lady suggests a president's wife, but here it is Eve, the first woman in the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: To evade is to escape or dodge something, which is what avoid means as a verb.

clue.text: Discharge from no team in a poor condition?

indicators.note: something in poor condition is out of shape, so the letters before are rearranged

parts.note: the four words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A medical-sounding discharge comes from a squad in bad shape.
explanation.definitionFit: An emanation is something that flows out or is given off from a source, a discharge or emission.

clue.text: Continental herdsman's dog

parts.note: a German is one kind of Continental European
a shepherd herds sheep

explanation.surface: A European herder's working dog.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is possessive in the surface but just joins wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The German shepherd is a large breed of dog, also called an Alsatian, used for police and herding work.
